memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they set out, and the terror of God fell on the towns all around them so that no one pursued them. Jacob and all the people with him came to Luz (that is, Bethel) in the land of Canaan. There he built an altar, and he called the place El Bethel, because it was there that God revealed himself to him when he was fleeing from his brother." - Gen 35:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After the massacre at Shechem, Jacob had feared reprisal from the surrounding peoples — he had said, "I and my household will be destroyed" (Gen 34:30). His family was vulnerable, few in number, travelling through hostile territory. Yet as they set out in obedience to God, we read that "the terror of God fell on the towns all around them so that no one pursued them." God Himself shielded them. The danger Jacob dreaded never fell.

There is a wonderful principle here: the path of obedience is the path of God's protection. When Jacob obeyed the call to return to Bethel, God went before him and held back every threat. The safest place in the world is the place of doing what God has said.

We sometimes hesitate to obey God because we fear the consequences — what we might lose, who might oppose us, what danger might follow. But when we step out in obedience, we step into God's care. He is able to restrain what threatens us and clear the way before us.

Arriving at Bethel, Jacob built an altar and named it El Bethel — "the God of Bethel." He worshipped the God who had met him there years before and had kept him ever since. When God brings you safely through, build your altar too, and worship the God who protects those who obey Him.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is fear of consequences keeping me from obeying God?
2. Do I trust that the path of obedience is the path of God's protection?
3. Is worship my response when God brings me safely through?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to obey You even when I fear the consequences. Thank You that You go before Your people and protect those who walk in Your ways. I worship You, the God who keeps me. Amen.
